method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children with high-count leukaemia are at risk of death or serious complications** from leukostasis/hyperviscosity. Hyperleukocytosis should prompt consideration of acute leukaemia.
claims.source_text: Children with high count leukaemia (hyperleukocytosis) are at risk of death or serious complications due to leukostasis/hyperviscosity syndrome … Hyperleukocytosis should prompt consideration of possible acute leukaemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Leukostasis** (symptomatic hyperleukocytosis) is a clinical diagnosis: respiratory distress, CNS abnormalities or other organ dysfunction attributed to hyperleukocytosis.
claims.source_text: Leukostasis (symptomatic hyperleukocytosis) is a clinical diagnosis in which respiratory distress, CNS abnormalities or other organ dysfunction is attributed to hyperleukocytosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complications:** ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke · pulmonary or renal thrombosis and infarction · tumour lysis syndrome · DIC. Their frequency depends on the type of leukaemia.
claims.source_text: Hyperleukocytosis is associated with serious and potentially fatal complications, including ischaemic and haemorrhagic strokes pulmonary or renal thrombosis and infarction tumour lysis syndrome coagulopathy: disseminated intravascular coagulation … The frequency of complications from hyperleukocytosis depends on the type of leukaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The main risks are bleeding or thrombosis, most often in the brain and lung.**
claims.source_text: The main risks are bleeding or thrombosis. Organs most frequently affected are the brain and lung
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask about** visual disturbance, dizziness, tinnitus, behaviour change and altered consciousness. **Look for** altered mental status, ataxia, papilloedema, retinal abnormalities, signs of raised intracranial pressure and increased work of breathing.
claims.source_text: History Visual disturbance, dizziness, tinnitus, behaviour changes, altered conscious state Examination Altered mental status, ataxia, papilloedema, retinal abnormalities, clinical signs of raised intracranial pressure Increased work of breathing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult oncology early; arrange retrieval to a tertiary centre and consider PICU for all children with hyperleukocytosis.**
claims.source_text: Early consultation with oncology is important, with retrieval to a tertiary centre and consideration of PICU for all children with hyperleukocytosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with oncology before further blood collection**, so time-sensitive investigations are prioritised.
claims.source_text: Discuss with oncology prior to further blood collection to help prioritise time sensitive investigations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods usually needed:** FBE and film · group and hold · UEC · LFT · CMP · LDH · coagulation screen with fibrinogen · uric acid · G6PD assay.
claims.source_text: Blood tests usually required include FBE and film Group and hold UEC LFT CMP LDH Coagulation screen, including fibrinogen. … Uric acid G6PD assay
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An adjusted coagulation tube may be needed if haematocrit is under 0.21** — discuss with the laboratory before taking blood.
claims.source_text: An adjusted coagulation tube may be required; if there is significant anaemia (haematocrit <0.21). Discuss with the laboratory prior to taking blood
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CXR; consider neuroimaging if there are neurological symptoms or signs.**
claims.source_text: Imaging CXR Consider neuroimaging, if neurological signs or symptoms present
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitoring:** continuous saturations (consider cardiac monitoring) · **4-hourly neuro obs** · **6-hourly FBE, UEC, CMP, uric acid** ± coagulation.
claims.source_text: Continuous saturations monitoring recommended. Consider cardiac monitoring 4 hourly neurological observations 6 hourly FBE, UEC, CMP, uric acid +/- coagulation studies
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start hyperhydration at 125 mL/m²/hr (or double maintenance) with no added potassium** — 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% dextrose.
claims.source_text: Commence hyperhydration at 125 mL/m2/hr (or double maintenance rate) without added potassium (0.9% NaCl with 5% Dextrose)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Platelet consumption can be extremely rapid; several platelet transfusions may be needed per day.**
claims.source_text: Platelet consumption can be extremely rapid, and multiple transfusions may be needed per day
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Correct coagulopathy: keep INR under 2.0, APTT under 80 and fibrinogen over 1.0.**
claims.source_text: Correct coagulopathy: maintain INR <2.0, APTT <80 and fibrinogen >1.0.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid red cell transfusion unless oncology suggests it, and then limit it to 5–10 mL/kg** to minimise hyperviscosity.
claims.source_text: Avoid red cell transfusion unless directed by oncology … Red cell transfusions should be avoided unless suggested by oncology, and limited to 5-10 mL/kg to minimise risk of hyperviscosity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.source_text: Oncology may recommend commencement of allopurinol or rasburicase
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Hyperleukocytosis' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Hyperleukocytosis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
